clue.text: Regular shape made of two metals

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, one metal
Be is the chemical symbol for beryllium, the second metal

explanation.surface: Someone describes a geometric solid fashioned from a pair of metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two metals' gives two chemical symbols, copper (Cu) and beryllium (Be), side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid with six identical square faces is the standard regular polyhedron.

clue.text: Explosive device set up by a group of soldiers gets large rodent

parts.note: a cap is a small percussion charge, as in a cap gun

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the following little word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
RA is the Royal Artillery, a regiment of soldiers

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers rigs a bomb and comes away with a huge rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns BY into YB in this down clue. RA, the Royal Artillery, is the usual crossword group of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American capybara is the biggest living species of rodent.

clue.text: Example of South African insect being eaten by another (though not the tail)

indicators.note: one insect swallowed by another means one word goes inside the other
the tail of a word is its last letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: another insect, a bug
the ant is a common insect

explanation.surface: A South African insect is devoured by a second bug, all but its tail end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though not the tail' drops the last letter of the second insect; 'being eaten by' puts the first insect inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu peoples are a large family of ethnic groups across southern Africa, so a member is one instance of a South African.

clue.text: Left shop after breaking item of cookware

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are broken apart and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a store after smashing a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges LEFT SHOP; 'after' only joins. The answer usually means a place of vice, but literally it is a cooking vessel for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshpot was originally a vessel in which meat was boiled, a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Guided round ring — cheetah, say, spotted

indicators.note: one word placed round the others, so it encloses them

parts.note: to lead someone is to guide them; past tense led
a ring is round like the letter O
a cheetah is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A cheetah is steered around a circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' wraps the ring and the big cat in the past tense of guide. 'Spotted' fits a cheetah's coat but is the definition, meaning found.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted something is to have found where it is.

clue.text: Regular payments indicated in Government regulations?

definitions.meaning: instructions to a bank to pay a fixed sum at set intervals
the permanent rules governing procedure in a parliament

explanation.surface: Direct-debit style payments are said to be set out in state rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indicated in' just links the two senses; the question mark flags the parliamentary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a bank mandate for repeated payments and the written rules of procedure in a legislature.

clue.text: I conspire to wreck such accuracy

indicators.note: wrecking the letters of the two words means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A plotter vows to sabotage someone's exactness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To wreck' rearranges I CONSPIRE; 'such' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness of measurement or execution is a synonym for accuracy.

clue.text: Love being embraced by a little vile thing

indicators.note: one word held inside another, as in an embrace

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance hugged by a small, nasty creature.
explanation.walkthrough: O (love, a nil score in tennis) goes inside TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A loathsome person or creature is called by the name of the warty amphibian.

clue.text: Stop the discussion and play a foreigner instead

definitions.meaning: to change the topic or say no more about it
an actor cast not as a citizen or subject of the realm but as an alien

explanation.surface: An actor halts a conversation by switching to playing an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'subject' as a citizen of a monarchy: drop that role and play a foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abandon a topic; read literally it means discard the role of a citizen.

clue.text: No main faults in embryonic membrane

indicators.note: faults in the letters show they are flawed and rearranged

explanation.surface: No serious defects appear in the membrane round a fetus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faults' rearranges NO MAIN; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the innermost sac enclosing the developing fetus.

clue.text: One aims and shoots wide

parts.note: sounds like a poor marksman, but describes a device pointed at a scene that takes wide-angle photographs

explanation.surface: A careless gunman points his weapon and misses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' is photographic and 'wide' is the broad sweep of the picture, not a missed target.
explanation.definitionFit: This device captures an extra-wide field of view in a single photograph.

clue.text: the Porn Squad?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'the Porn Squad? (9)', starting lower case with no definition; the start is missing and no source gives it.

clue.text: Parliament regularly finishing early

indicators.note: a word that finishes early has its last letter cut off

parts.note: something done regularly, every day, is daily

explanation.surface: MPs routinely knock off before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' looks like the subject; it is the definition, the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil Éireann is the lower house of the Irish legislature.

clue.text: Take out smoothness from much of make-up used by woman

indicators.note: most of a word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: rouge is a red cosmetic
hen is an informal word for a woman

explanation.surface: Removing the sleekness from heavy cosmetics a woman wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' trims the cosmetic's last letter; 'used by' only links it to the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a surface coarse is to remove its smooth finish.

clue.text: Lake wet us all in storm, right?

indicators.note: the letters are tossed about as if in a storm

explanation.surface: A lake soaked everyone during a storm, didn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In storm' rearranges WET US ALL; R for right follows. ULLSWATER is a lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullswater is the second-largest body of fresh water in the Cumbrian Lake District.

clue.text: Bird detected from noise around a French Lake

indicators.note: one word goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
un is French for a
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird is picked out by its call near a lake in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts the French article and the lake abbreviation inside the noise; 'detected from' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunlin is a small wading sandpiper of shores and estuaries.

clue.text: Source of mild stimulant for 60s pop fan, we hear

indicators.note: the clue's words are spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a fanatic for the 1960s Liverpool band, a Beatles devotee or nut

explanation.surface: A sixties music devotee is said to be a source of a gentle high.
explanation.walkthrough: A Beatle nut, a fan of the Beatles, sounds like the areca seed that is chewed.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca seed is chewed across South Asia for its mildly stimulating effect.

clue.text: Reduced Cabinet had finished business

indicators.note: the word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard or cabinet
the contraction 'd stands for had

explanation.surface: A smaller Cabinet had concluded its affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests the government; it is a cupboard, CLOSET, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that is shut has stopped trading, so it has ceased business.

clue.text: Beautiful girl "cut" boy after receiving one's scorn

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first in the answer
the quoted word cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: one word takes in another, so it goes inside

parts.note: Dan is a boy's name
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lovely girl snubs a lad after taking in a person's contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'cut' trims the last letter of the slang word for a beauty; 'receiving' puts one inside the boy, who comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt or a feeling that something is beneath you is a synonym for scorn.

clue.text: Go off in disgust, following no clue being sorted out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: letters being sorted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone storms off, having no idea how to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: F, for following, leads an anagram of NO CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm out with exaggerated movements of annoyance is to leave in a huff.

clue.text: Force advanced, capturing capital of Uganda without hesitation

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: one word takes another prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it, so lent

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: An army pushed forward and took the Ugandan capital without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Uganda' looks like Kampala; it is just U, which LENT captures.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking smoothly and easily, without stumbling, is the sense here.

clue.text: Bits of surgical wadding with blood attached?

definitions.text: Bits of surgical wadding with blood attached?

indicators.note: the first bits of each word, their opening letters

parts.note: AB is one of the human blood groups

explanation.surface: Fragments of hospital cotton wool smeared with blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'surgical wadding' come before AB, a blood group; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of absorbent material used in surgery to mop blood is the item described.

clue.text: Political comment is done but needs editing

indicators.note: editing reworks the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's remark is finished but must be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs editing' rearranges IS DONE BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, quotable extract from a politician's speech, clipped for broadcast, is the sense.

clue.text: Gold invested in plant making key component

indicators.note: to invest one thing in another is to put it inside

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold is put into a plant that makes a vital part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a piano key, not crucial; OR is gold in heraldry, which 'invested in' puts inside the climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with elephant tusk material.

clue.text: Attempt is cracked up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: someone who is cracked, mad, is bats

explanation.surface: An effort has fallen apart completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is cracked' means is crazy, BATS; read up the grid it becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something, an attempt, is a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Naturally suited for being carried off by a Lord, by the sound of it!

indicators.note: the words are spoken and give a phrase that sounds alike

parts.words: being carried off by a Lord
parts.note: something carried off by a lord is borne away to his country house, the manor

explanation.surface: Someone is ideally fitted for being whisked away by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borne to the manor' sounds like the Shakespearean phrase; 'for' only links. The phrase is often misheard as 'manor born'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Hamlet means accustomed by birth, at ease as if from upbringing.

clue.text: Opening of piece of music includes it for a singer

indicators.note: one piece includes another, holding it inside

parts.note: the opening of a written score is bar one
taken as written

explanation.surface: The start of a composition contains it, for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a first letter; it is bar one, the first bar of a score, which takes in IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass belongs to this kind of vocalist.

clue.text: It's an island to you, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows the letters backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone thinks again about an island near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns TO YE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot, or ait, is a small isle in a river, especially the Thames.
